heading: Menu items that open a page
body:
An item with a `route` opens a page of the app in the same window. Each item has an `id`, a `label`, the `route` and an optional `shortcut`. An item has exactly one of `route` or `action`. The `route` must be a static page of the app, without a query or a fragment, such as `/help`. A shortcut has one lowercase letter or digit and always includes `command`; it may add `control`, `option` and `shift`. On Linux and Windows, `command` is Ctrl, `option` is Alt and `shift` is Shift. A shortcut that uses `control` has no keyboard shortcut there, because Ctrl is already `command`; the item still works from the menu. There are at most 64 items in all menus, and ids and shortcuts must be unique. A wrong item (a bad id, label or shortcut, both `route` and `action`, or neither) stops the build with `TY1601`.

Opening a page loads a new document. The services of the old page stop, and the new page starts with fresh services. Use a menu action when the item must keep the state of the page.
